intro: My research focuses on the innermost regions of active galactic nuclei (AGN) — the hot corona, the accretion flow, and the obscuring material that surrounds growing supermassive black holes. I use X-ray spectroscopy together with radiative-transfer simulations to turn observed spectra into physical pictures of these environments.

topics.title: Close environments of supermassive black holes
topics.text: Mapping the circumnuclear gas and dust of accreting supermassive black holes: its geometry, column density, and how it shapes what we observe across obscured and unobscured AGN.

topics.title: X-ray spectral modeling
topics.text: Developing realistic X-ray spectral models with ray-tracing radiative-transfer simulations, so that features like the Fe Kα line and its Compton shoulder can be used as physical probes rather than fitting conveniences.

topics.title: The Fe Kα Compton shoulder
topics.text: Studying the Compton shoulder of the Fe Kα line as a diagnostic of the density, geometry, and motion of the reprocessing material in accreting supermassive black holes.

topics.title: Multi-wavelength views of AGN coronae
topics.text: Connecting millimeter and X-ray emission of accreting black holes to understand the nature of the corona, and preparing these diagnostics for the next generation of X-ray observatories.
